The test image shows a tomato stem split open longitudinally, revealing:
- Hollow, dry white/tan pith inside the stem
- Dark black irregular bodies (sclerotia) visible inside the cavity
- Brown/necrotic external stem tissue
- Dead/dying surrounding plant tissue

This pattern — hollow stem with internal black sclerotia — strongly suggests **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference confirms Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot — showing stem collapse and necrosis. The test image is the internal view of the same disease: a split stem showing the hollow pith with dark black irregular sclerotia inside, which is the textbook hallmark of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (timber rot). No other class produces large black sclerotia inside hollow tomato stems like this.
